items.title: Frank Alkyer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Orleans, Louisiana, January 10, 2020
items.q: as a result of people like Bill Gottlieb and Nat Hentoff and Dan Morgenstern that the artists’ voice is front and center in those pieces

ctx.x: Did you have a good relationship with Nat Hentoff? © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-

Yeah, I did. But I always wanted him — his time at DownBeat I don’t think ended well back in the 50s, which is a recurring theme. I like to think it hasn’t happened as often under my tenure there. But there were turf wars, there were people, but Nat Hentoff, I started reading Nat Hentoff not necessarily in DownBeat but when I lived in New York and the Village Voice when he was covering the Supreme Court. And I loved his writing. You know the Village Voice was my paper in New York City. That was the thing that I…

Yeah, no. We got to know him a little bit. I did an interview with him and it was a challenge. Not ‘cause he was — he was very nice. But he was Nat Hentoff. And I felt like everything I’m asking him I hope is not like silly.
